title: What number does this Egyptian numeral stand for?
description: An Egyptian numeral is read by adding the value of every symbol in it. The video reads a carving of three lotuses, four heels and six strokes, and a landmark with no symbols adds nothing. Keeko's doubt is that the counts can be read side by side like digits.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the value of every symbol, because each Egyptian symbol keeps its value wherever it sits. A landmark with no symbols adds nothing to the total. Watch for students who read the counts as digits in places.

source: An Egyptian numeral shows 3 lotuses, 4 heels and 6 strokes.
video_script.why: The child sees that an Egyptian numeral is read by adding the values of its symbols, not by reading the counts as digits.
video_script.substitution: Find the value of each kind of symbol, then add the values of all the symbols.
video_script.anchor: a carving of 3 lotuses, 4 heels and 6 strokes in a row
video_script.wrong_answer: read it as three hundred forty six
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads the counts three, four and six side by side as three hundred forty six. A lotus is worth one thousand, so three lotuses alone are more than that, and the counts are not digits in places.
video_script.payoff_line: The numeral stands for three thousand forty six
never_show: the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: no coils, so no hundreds are added
video_script.design: One idea: add the value of every symbol. The carving stays on the stage and each kind of symbol lights up in turn with its value.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a carving of 3 lotuses, 4 heels and 6 strokes appears; a question mark appears

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about reading an Egyptian numeral.
<bookmark mark='carve'/>A carving shows three lotuses, four heels and six strokes.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What number does the carving stand for in our system?

beats.on_screen: the carving holds still and the question mark glows

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board and the question mark glows

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the carving moves to the stage; the values are joined to the symbols: stroke 1, heel 10, coil 100, lotus 1000

marks.vals: the stroke and the heel are joined to one and ten
marks.vals2: the coil and the lotus are joined to one hundred and one thousand
marks.keep: an arrow shows that each symbol keeps its value wherever it sits

narration: <bookmark mark='vals'/>A stroke is one and a heel is ten.
<bookmark mark='vals2'/>A coil is one hundred and a lotus is one thousand.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Every symbol keeps its value, so we add the value of each symbol.

beats.on_screen: Given: an Egyptian numeral with 3 lotuses, 4 heels and 6 strokes

marks.given: the facts are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, an Egyptian numeral with three lotuses, four heels and six strokes.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number the numeral stands for

marks.find: the words To find are written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number that the numeral stands for.

marks.m1: the three lotuses light up, each with 1000 beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, find the total value of the three lotuses on the carving.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>A lotus is worth one thousand in this system.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Three lotuses together make three thousand.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: no coils, so no hundreds are added; 4 heels: 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 40

marks.m3: the coil place on the carving is shown empty, with a note that no hundreds are added
marks.m4: the four heels light up, each with 10 beside it, and 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 40 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, look at the coils and the heels on the carving.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>There are no coils, so no hundreds are added.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Four heels together make a value of forty.

marks.m5: the six strokes light up, each with 1 beside it, and 6 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, look at the strokes at the end of the carving.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Six strokes together make a value of six.

marks.m6: the three values 3000, 40 and 6 slide together into one sum

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, add the values of all the symbols.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>Three thousand plus forty plus six.

marks.chk: the carving is read back: 3 lotuses, 4 heels and 6 strokes give 3000, 40 and 6

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The numeral stands for three thousand forty six.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Check by reading the carving back. The three lotuses give three thousand, the four heels give forty, and the six strokes give six.

beats.on_screen: Keeko appears beside the board with a raised hand
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 346; the three lotuses light up with 1000 on each; the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the counts 3, 4 and 6 side by side as 346
marks.lotus: the three lotuses light up with 1000 on each
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the sum 3000 + 40 + 6 is shown

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we should read it as three hundred forty six.
<bookmark mark='lotus'/>Each lotus is one thousand, so the three lotuses alone are far more than that.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The counts are not digits in places. We add the value of every symbol.
